bull.b: The shift to strongly positive operating and free cash flow in 2024 through TTM provides meaningful internal funding capacity. This supports investment in products, customer growth and infrastructure while reducing reliance on external capital, although sustaining the improvement remains important.

Faster customer acquisition combined with better-than-expected CAC and higher revenue per customer indicates improving marketing efficiency and monetization. These trends can strengthen lifetime value and support scalable growth across DraftKings’ regulated digital gaming platforms.

Rapid Predictions adoption broadens DraftKings’ digital wagering offering and creates an additional engagement channel alongside Sportsbook and iGaming. The company’s exchange launch and expanding market coverage could improve product differentiation and long-term customer lifetime value.

bear.b: Debt exceeding three times equity leaves DraftKings more sensitive to earnings volatility and reduces financial flexibility. A highly leveraged capital structure may constrain investment choices, increase pressure during weaker operating periods, and make consistent cash generation especially important.

Despite substantial multi-year revenue growth and improved gross margins, DraftKings has not yet demonstrated consistently durable profitability. The return to a net loss and negative operating profit suggests that growth, investment and operating costs continue to offset revenue scale.

The large planned Predictions investment can weigh on near-term earnings and cash conversion before the product reaches its targeted scale. Regulatory questions also create uncertainty over rollout timing, market access and how quickly DraftKings can capture the platform’s potential.
